basis.governing_question: Why do property and health claims take too long to settle, and what claims operating model should Atlântico Seguros move to?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Find why property and health claims take too long to settle, compared with the 2024 motor claims results.

gate.label: Diagnostic readout
gate.decision: Does the steering group accept the diagnostic findings on property and health claims?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Define the claims operating model for property and health claims and the recommendations the Board will receive.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Are the report and Board presentation ready for the March 15, 2027 Board meeting?

workstreams.name: Claims process mapping
workstreams.answers: How do property and health claims flow from opening to settlement, and where does time accumulate?
activities: Map the property and health claims steps and handoffs
Trace a sample of claims from opening to settlement
Review claims procedures and handling documents

workstreams.name: Claims staff interviews
workstreams.answers: Where do the people who handle property and health claims, and their managers, see delays and their causes?
activities: Interview the people who handle property and health claims
Interview the COO and Head of Claims on the lean program
Synthesize interviews into delay causes by claim type

workstreams.name: Settlement time baseline
workstreams.answers: How long do property and health claims take to settle today, and how satisfied are customers?
activities: Measure settlement time by claim type from operational data
Gather customer satisfaction results by claim type
Record current levels for both success criteria

workstreams.name: Delay root causes
workstreams.answers: What causes the delays in property and health claims, and what separates them from the 2024 motor improvement?
activities: Review the 2024 lean program documents and results
Compare property and health with motor claims results
Test candidate delay causes and draft the readout findings

workstreams.name: Claims model options
workstreams.answers: Which claims operating model options address the diagnosed causes of delay in property and health claims?
activities: Set option criteria with the COO and Head of Claims
Define claims operating model options for the workshop
Frame structure, roles, process and governance per option

workstreams.name: Model impact assessment
workstreams.answers: How would each option, and then the chosen model, change settlement time and customer satisfaction?
activities: Estimate settlement time effects of each option
Assess customer satisfaction risks of each option
Test the chosen model against both success criteria

workstreams.name: Detailed model design
workstreams.answers: How does the chosen operating model work in detail across process, roles and governance?
activities: Design process, roles and governance of the chosen option
Validate the design with claims handlers and managers
Check the design against the current claims IT system

workstreams.name: Board recommendations
workstreams.answers: What recommendations and supporting case will the Board receive on the claims operating model?
activities: Draft the report with findings, model and recommendations
Prepare the Board presentation for the March 2027 meeting
Review the draft with the COO and Head of Claims

deliverables.name: Property and health claims process baseline
Interview synthesis of delay causes by claim type
Settlement time and customer satisfaction baseline
Diagnostic findings on property and health claim delays
Settlement time and satisfaction effects by option
Chosen model tested against both success criteria
Detailed design of the chosen claims operating model
Written report on the claims operating model
Board presentation for the March 2027 Board meeting

events.label: Kick-off
events.decision: Does the steering group confirm the scope, team and calendar?
agenda: Present the objectives and the two-phase plan
Align on the project team and the meeting calendar
Confirm scope, success criteria and the Board date

events.label: Workshop 1: first findings
events.decision: Which delay causes should the root cause analysis prioritize?
agenda: Present the property and health claims process baseline
Review interview synthesis of delay causes by claim type
Discuss which causes need root cause analysis

events.label: Diagnostic readout
events.purpose: Close Phase 1 on the diagnostic findings
events.decision: Does the steering group accept the diagnostic findings on property and health claims?
agenda: Present diagnostic findings on property and health
Review the settlement time and satisfaction baseline
Discuss the comparison with the 2024 motor claims results

events.label: Workshop 2: model options
events.purpose: Review model options and their effects
events.decision: Which claims operating model option should be detailed and tested?
agenda: Present the claims operating model options
Review settlement time and satisfaction effects by option
Align on the option to take into detailed design

events.label: Final readout
events.purpose: Prepare for the March 15 Board meeting
events.decision: Are the report and Board presentation ready for the March 15, 2027 Board meeting?
agenda: Present chosen model tested against both criteria
Review the detailed design and the written report
Decide if the Board materials are ready for March 15

deadline.text: Recommendations presented to the Board on March 15, 2027

architect_notes: Length is an estimate of 14 to 18 weeks, resting on the archetype's typical phase lengths, two claim lines and the 19 weeks available.
Not covered by the phases: ASF, new guidance on claims-handling response times for non-life insurers. Confirm whether it is in scope.
The success criteria name a settlement-time reduction that an assessment cannot measure; confirm they become targets in the recommendations, not results to track.
